text:
Kai: Heads-up — infra repo GHA is stalling repeated terraform apply jobs. Concurrency group is 1 so everything queues. Seen this since ~6:40am PT. Anyone else?
Anna: Yep saw it. cache-restore step failing intermittently then runner hangs waiting for terraform lock.
Sam: Getting this in the runner logs: 
```
Restoring cache 'gha-terraform-cache'... failed (403)
Error: request failed, status 403
...
Terraform apply waiting for lock: plan-queue: pending
```
Anna: The 403 looks like cache service rate-limiting our self-hosted runner IPs after the autoscaler churns nodes.
Maya: Also noticed a second symptom: GKE GPU nodepool autoscaler is creating a node in europe-west1 for some workloads and the Terraform resource waits for node registration -> GH action times out after 30m, leaves the concurrency slot locked.
Jamal: That matches recent alerts — node provisioning taking 20–40m when GPUs requested + regional quota checks. Costly churn too.
Kai: So two problems stacking: 1) cache restore flakiness leaves runner steps in limbo, 2) serial CI lock (concurrency:1) means a stuck run blocks everyone.
Anna: Quick mitigation idea: temporarily increase concurrency to 2 for infra CI and add a workflow-level timeout/retry for cache-restore. Then we can kill stuck run without blocking others.
Sam: Agree. Also add a small wrapper around terraform apply to detect long-running locks and force-unlock after TTL but with manual approval for apply in prod.
Maya: For the GPU provisioning side — we should pin nodepool region in the terraform job or bail earlier if quota errors show. Right now the autoscaler picks other regions, which trips up our static GKE kubeconfig expectation.
Jamal: I'll open a quick PR to fail fast on quota/region mismatch and emit clear error so the job doesn't hang.
Kai: Can someone post the failing workflow id and a snippet for ops to kill?
Anna: Workflow run: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/actions/runs/35421987. ID 35421987.
Anna: If you need the command to cancel: `gh run cancel 35421987 --repo redwood-inference/infra`
Sam: I'm going to drain the runner pool that kept re-registering and reboot the autoscaler controller. Will post status in 10m.
Oncall-Bot: Incident created: #CI-Blocker-177245 — ticket INFRA-1123 assigned to eng-infra oncall.
Maya: Post-mitigation action items: add cache restore retry (3x), increase GHA timeout for infra workflows to 60m, add worker-side lock TTL + metric to alert when locks exceed 15m, and add region/quota checks before nodepool create.
Kai: Sounds good. Anna, can you do the cache retry + timeout? Sam, runner pool. Jamal, PR for fail-fast region check. I'll follow up with a short doc on changing concurrency and safe unlock procedure.
Anna: On it. I'll open a PR and include test job that simulates cache 403.
Sam: Runner reboot done, garbage cached restored for new jobs. Killed run 35421987. New queued job started and passed lint.
Jamal: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/849 — adds preflight region/quota check + clearer errors.
Kai: Great. Recording this in postmortem draft. TL;DR: cache rate-limits + long GPU node provisioning + serial GHA concurrency = CI deadlock. Fixes: retries, timeouts, fail-fast checks, TTL for locks, and consider reserving a small pool of warm GPU nodes to avoid long cold starts (cost vs reliability tradeoff).
Maya: Note on cost: warm pool of 1–2 GPUs in each primary region estimated +$6k/mo but reduces blocked runs and manual toil. Bring to finance if we go that route.
Anna: Closing loop: new infra workflow timeout pushed, cache retry in PR, and monitoring alert added for lock age > 15m. I'll post PR links once merged. :thumbsup:
Kai: Thanks all — archiving thread when PRs land.
